outcome: Incidence of hypertensive disorders and subtypes
Maternal intensive care or high-dependency unit admission
cohort: Pregnant women in Victoria, Australia from 2010 to 2017
finding: While the incidence of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy remained stable over time, hypertensive disorders were associated with increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, with the worst outcomes observed in women with superimposed and early preterm preeclampsia.
mod_finding: Compared to pregnancies without hypertension, hypertensive disorders were associated with medically-initiated birth and cesarean section.
